unit.title: Inception & “Build Just Enough Process”
unit.moc: the 4 core terms — the core principle — what it does/doesn't — the 7-step loop — the name

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 1 — gate
checkpoint.prompt: Reproduce the 4 core terms and the core principle, and name what the tribunal is NOT. Write a short verdict.

facts.text: The 4 core terms: **the Living Tribunal** (the system) → **A Sitting** = One Problem Run → **Quorum** = The Vote (3–5 Models) → **Convergence** = The Final Verdict. The `hub` CLI runs the process; the model is just the engine.

exercises.prompt: One problem run through the tribunal is called:
The multi-model vote over that problem is:
Match each term to its meaning.

lessons.title: Core Principle: Build Just Enough Process

facts.text: Formalize Thinly = Build Just Enough Process: the value is discipline (independence, grounding, recorded dissent), not machinery. This document + the intake template + the ledger + the `hub` CLI = the whole system.
The habit already paid real dividends: it caught an AI's wrong Cloudflare/Prisma/Neon claims, audited a session report, and shipped a migration blueprint — more validation than most tools get.

exercises.prompt: Formalize Thinly means the value is ___ , not the machinery.
Which of these is NOT part of “the whole system”?
The tribunal's habit has already caught a wrong model claim and audited a session report.

lessons.title: What the Tribunal Does (and Doesn't Do)

facts.text: The tribunal takes a problem from any session, routes the SAME brief through 2–5 independent model lanes, forces them to challenge each other, grounds the result in the second brain + fresh docs, and returns ONE converged, evidence-cited answer.

It is NOT: a build environment (it returns verdicts/blueprints, not commits), a chat playground, an agent orchestrator for long-running work, a replacement for reading primary docs, or a destination for lab data or secrets.

exercises.prompt: Which is a true statement about what the tribunal returns?

options: a way to route the same brief to independent lanes
grounded in the second brain + fresh docs
a build environment that returns commits
a way to force lanes to challenge each other

exercises.prompt: Which statement VIOLATES the tribunal's stated scope?
exercises.scenario: A new team member proposes using the tribunal as a destination for lab data and secrets.
options: grounding the result in the second brain
routing the same brief to independent lanes
storing lab data and secrets with the tribunal

lessons.title: The 7-Step Loop: Intake → Triage → Ground → Route → Converge → Verify → Record

facts.text: The 7-step loop: Intake → Triage → Ground → Route (blind) → Converge → Verify → Record. Independence is the product: each lane sees the SAME brief and no lane sees another's output until convergence.
Verify means against the artifact the user runs — run it, grep the repo, read the vendor doc. Never model agreement alone.

exercises.prompt: Put the 7 loop steps in order.
What does “verify” mean in the loop?
options: checking against the artifact the user runs

lessons.title: The Name: Quorum — Why It Was Chosen

facts.text: “Quorum” was real Claude's proposal and it names the property that makes the hub work — you need a quorum of independent voices, not one. “Crossbench” is the runner-up.

exercises.prompt: Which name was recommended, and why?
options: PolyModel Hub — because it is generic
Quorum — because it names the independence property
Sounding Board — because it is evocative

exercises.prompt: The name “Quorum” was proposed by real Claude.
